history.dynasty: Cheras (renovation 2nd-5th century CE); later contributions from Pandyas and Nayak kings
history.period: Ancient (origins over 2,000 years per tradition; built structure 2nd-5th century CE)
history.summary: The famous Palani HILL temple, one of the Six Abodes (Arupadai Veedu / Padai Veedu) of Murugan and the third of the army camps. Perched on the 450-ft Sivagiri hill, the idol depicts Murugan as a youthful ascetic recluse with a staff (dhanda), crafted of navapashanam (nine herbal-mineral substances) and attributed to the Siddha sage Bogar. Legend: Murugan withdrew here as a hermit after losing the gnana-palam (fruit of knowledge) to Ganesha; the hillock was carried from Kailasha by Idumban at sage Agastya's command. Mentioned as Thiruaavinankudi in Sangam literature (Tirumurukarruppatai of Nakkeerar); sung by Arunagirinathar. Kavadi ritual tradition began here; tonsuring and Palani Panchamritam (GI-tagged prasadam) are famed. Managed by the HRCE Department. NOTE: distinct from the foothill Thiruavinankudi temple (seq 2278) - separate shrine, separate record.

name: Arulmigu Dhandayuthapani Swamy Temple
town_description: A temple town in Dindigul district in the foothills of the Palani Hills (Western Ghats), about 100 km southeast of Coimbatore and 122 km northwest of Madurai.
tradition: Shaivite-affiliated Murugan worship; Sivagamam (per temple festival invitation)

travel.airport: Coimbatore International Airport, about 100 km northwest (distance verify)
travel.road: Hilltop reached via 693 sacred steps, electric winch railway, or rope car; the town is on the Dindigul-Coimbatore route

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Thaipusam (Jan-Feb) is the grandest festival with massive crowds
